sections.h2: Where does Brazoria County keep its deed and lien records?
sections.html:
The Brazoria County Clerk's Recording Department keeps them, in the Administration Building at 237 East Locust, Suite 102, Angleton, TX 77515. The recording and vitals line is 979-864-1059. Angleton is the county seat, and trustee sale notices are posted at the courthouse there.

The clerk's site runs a searchable database of real property records that you can use from home or on public computers at the Angleton office. New users create a login and answer a verification email before searching. The office adds that its clerks are recorders, not qualified examiners of the records, so they will not run a title search for you. The online database is also not the official repository, and some information is redacted as state law requires.

  • Plain copies: $1.00 per page
  • Certified copies: $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document, mailed by regular post only
  • Copy requests go through an online application, and payment follows an approval email

sections.h2: What does recording a document cost in Brazoria County?
sections.html:
A one-page deed costs $25.00 to record in Brazoria County. That total is a $10.00 records management fee, a $10.00 records archive fee and a $5.00 first-page fee, and each additional page is $4.00. Names indexed beyond the first five add $0.25 each.

Document or serviceBrazoria County fee
First page of a recorded instrument$25.00
Each additional page$4.00
Federal tax lien or release$30.00
Plat, first page$120.00
Each additional plat page$100.00
Trustee notice of sale$8.00
Assumed name filing$23.00
Expedited service fee$5.00 plus the mail service

Source: Brazoria County Clerk, Recording and Vitals Fees.

Penalties catch careless filers. A deed with no grantee mailing address owes the greater of $25 or twice the filing fee on top of normal charges. The fee for a page doubles if names are not typed or printed under each signature, and doubles again for a page lacking a heading that identifies the document type.

sections.h2: What formatting rules does the Brazoria County Clerk enforce?
sections.html:
The county clerk publishes a long checklist, and a deed that misses a line can be rejected. Since January 1, 2026, anyone presenting a real property document in person must show photo ID to the clerk, under Local Government Code 191.010.

  • Original signatures, with each signer's name printed or typed beneath, and a notary acknowledgment with a clear, dark seal
  • English language, or a certified translation attached
  • White paper between 8.5 x 11 and 8.5 x 14 inches, with type of at least 8 point in black or blue ink
  • A 3 inch top margin on page one and a heading naming the document type
  • A legal description showing the property lies in Brazoria County, or a reference to a prior recording that does
  • The Notice of Confidentiality Rights in 12 point bold type or 12 point capitals on any transfer to or from an individual

The county page also explains Senate Bill 30, effective September 1, 2021, which gives an owner a court process to have discriminatory restrictions in old records reviewed, with no filing fee under the statute.

E-recording is open only to filers qualified under Local Government Code 195.003, through Simplifile, CSC/Ingeo, Nationwide Title Clearing, ePN, Indecomm or hopdox. Re-recording an e-recorded deed requires a certified copy or the original with the first and last pages of the e-recorded version attached.

sections.h2: What other services does the Brazoria County Clerk price?
sections.html:
The fee page lists several mail and data services beyond a basic recording. Expedited service is $5.00 plus the mail option you choose, which is $5.00 for 3 day priority post or $30.00 for FedEx overnight. Title plants that want bulk data can buy daily, weekly or two week CDs of images and indices at $6.00, $8.00 and $12.00, or daily and weekly FTP at $3.00 and $5.00.

Faxed pages cost $1.00 each plus a usage charge of $1.00 in the calling area or $2.00 outside it, and the clerk says vital records cannot be faxed. Copies of 11 x 17 pages are $2.00 each, and a 24 x 36 plat or map copy is $5.00 a page.

sections.h2: What is Brazoria County like, and how does the land affect records?
sections.html:
Brazoria County is a 1,407 square mile Gulf Coast county at the mouth of the Brazos River, and flood and hurricane exposure shapes how its land is held and insured. The Handbook of Texas notes 52 inches of annual rainfall, a long list of historic hurricanes and floods, and soils that are productive when well drained.

The county was created in 1836, and Angleton replaced the town of Brazoria as seat in 1896. Pearland is the largest city, and Brazosport is a community of nine cities that includes Lake Jackson, Clute, Freeport and Surfside Beach. State highways 6, 35, 36 and 288 serve the area. The economy leans on petrochemicals, with Dow Chemical arriving at Freeport in 1939, plus agriculture, fishing and tourism.

Census figures show a fast-growing, higher income market:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 419,080, up 12.6 percent from April 2020
  • Housing units: 162,298, with 74.1 percent owner occupied
  • Median value of owner occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $301,600
  • Median household income: $97,993, and mean commute 30.6 minutes
  • Median gross rent: $1,454

sections.h2: How does the appraisal district fit in for Brazoria County owners?
sections.html:
The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, at 500 North Chenango in Angleton, sets the value and handles exemptions, while the clerk records the deed. Its home page reminds owners that notices of appraised value are due by April 1 for single-family homes and May 1 for other property, or as soon after as practical.

The district also describes a homestead audit program under Senate Bill 1801, which requires each residence homestead exemption to be reviewed at least once every five tax years. Owners who get no letter need not file again. The Tax Assessor-Collector's office, at 111 E. Locust in Angleton, is listed at 979-864-1320 for tax bills.

On the state side, the school district homestead exemption is $140,000, and owners 65 or older or disabled receive $60,000 more. A tax lien attaches every January 1, and delinquent taxes after January 31 carry penalty and interest. When a house is sold, the recorded deed is what moves ownership on the appraisal rolls, so file it promptly after closing.

sections.h2: What recording problems slow a Brazoria County sale?
sections.html:
The usual culprits are missing notary details, a legal description that does not match the prior deed, and unreleased liens. A release of a paid-off lien is itself a recordable instrument, so ask the lender for it in writing and confirm it appears in the clerk's index.

Inherited houses need extra proof. The State Law Library says an affidavit of heirship is a sworn, court-unverified statement filed with the county clerk, and no law forces third parties to accept it. An order from the probate court, or a transfer on death deed recorded before the owner's death, gives a buyer firmer footing.

Foreclosure timing also shows up in these records. A notice of sale must be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk at least 21 days before the first-Tuesday auction, and Brazoria County charges $8.00 for a trustee notice.

faqs.q: What is the first-page recording fee in Brazoria County?
faqs.a: It is $25.00 in total, made of a $10.00 records management fee, a $10.00 records archive fee and a $5.00 first-page fee. Each additional page costs $4.00.

faqs.q: Do I need photo ID to record a deed in Brazoria County?
faqs.a: Yes, for in-person filings. Since January 1, 2026 anyone presenting a document for the real property records must provide photo ID to the clerk, per Local Government Code 191.010.

faqs.q: Can Brazoria County staff search the records for me?
faqs.a: No. The clerks are recorders and are not qualified examiners, so you search the online database yourself or use the public computers at 237 East Locust in Angleton.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a Brazoria County deed?
faqs.a: Search the database for the document number and page count, then submit the online copy application. Certified copies cost $1.00 per page plus $5.00 per document and are sent by regular mail.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed has no grantee mailing address?
faqs.a: The clerk adds a penalty fee. Texas Property Code 11.003 sets it at the greater of $25 or twice the statutory filing fee, charged on top of the regular recording cost.
